articles.title: Tusker Face Al Ahli in Decisive CAF Confederation Cup Return Leg
articles.desc: Tusker host Sudan's Al Ahli Wad Madani at Nyayo today, with the CAF Confederation Cup tie level 2-2 after the first leg.
articles.content:
Tusker FC will take on Sudanese side Al Ahli Wad Madani at Nyayo National Stadium on Saturday as they fight for a place in the next round of the CAF Confederation Cup.


The two sides enter the return leg level at 2-2 on aggregate after an eventful first meeting in Kigali on September 6. Tusker had appeared to be in control after taking a two-goal lead, but Al Ahli fought back to force a draw.


The result leaves everything to be decided in Nairobi, with Tusker now holding home advantage ahead of the decisive second leg.


The Brewers will be looking to make that advantage count as they attempt to continue their continental campaign. A victory would send Tusker through to the next stage, while another draw would leave the qualification outcome dependent on the competition's tie-breaking procedures.


Tusker's collapse in the first leg has also increased the pressure on the Kenyan side. After leading 2-0, the team allowed Al Ahli to recover and level the match, with coach Julien Mette pointing to inexperience and poor decisions as factors behind the result.


The return fixture therefore presents Tusker with an opportunity to correct what went wrong in the opening encounter.


The match is scheduled to take place at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi, giving Tusker the backing of a home crowd as they seek to progress in the CAF Confederation Cup.


For Kenyan football, Tusker's progress would provide another opportunity for a local club to remain involved in continental competition. The Brewers will now need to turn their first-leg performance into a complete result when the two sides meet again.


With the aggregate score level, there is little separating the teams going into the return leg. Tusker's ability to avoid another second-half collapse and make the most of their chances could determine who advances.

articles.title: FKF Meets Clubs as 2026/27 League Start Remains Uncertain
articles.desc: FKF held talks with clubs on September 2 as Kenya's 2026/27 top-flight season remains affected by a dispute over league rules.
articles.content:
Football Kenya Federation (FKF) held a fresh meeting with top-flight clubs on Wednesday, September 2, as uncertainty continued to surround the start of the 2026/27 Kenyan Premier League season.

The meeting brought together representatives of league clubs and FKF officials as the federation seeks to address key issues affecting preparations for the new campaign. FKF Chief Executive Officer Dennis Gicheru and Leagues and Competitions Head Frank Ogolla were reported to have led the discussions.

The talks came after the start of the new Kenyan Premier League season was disrupted by a legal dispute over the regulations governing promotion and relegation.

FKF had initially planned for the new season to begin in August, but the opening round of fixtures was postponed as the federation, clubs and other stakeholders continued consultations.

The dispute has centred on which FKF rules should govern the 2026/27 season and how promotion and relegation should be handled.

A High Court clarification has indicated that FKF can run its national leagues under the 2019 FKF Rules and Regulations, which remain unaffected by the current petition. The 2019 rules include a mandatory promotion and relegation playoff, an issue that has been central to the ongoing disagreement.

FKF President Hussein Mohammed has also acknowledged the need for further consultations with clubs before a clear way forward is agreed.

The federation's latest meeting is therefore significant for Kenyan football because clubs, players and supporters are still waiting for confirmation of when the 2026/27 campaign will officially begin.

The uncertainty has also affected clubs' preparations. Teams normally use the period before the start of a new season to finalise squads, prepare match strategies and plan their competitive schedules. With the league programme disrupted, clubs are instead waiting for clarity on the regulations and the new kick-off arrangements.

For football fans, the situation means another delay in the return of regular top-flight action involving clubs such as Gor Mahia, AFC Leopards, Tusker and Kenya Police.

Wednesday's talks represent a fresh attempt to bring stakeholders together, but FKF is yet to confirm whether the discussions will immediately lead to a new start date for the league.

The next decisions by the federation and the outcome of the legal process will be closely watched as Kenyan football seeks a resolution and a stable start to the 2026/27 season.

articles.title: Omanyala Ends 2026 Season Early After Heel Injury
articles.desc: Ferdinand Omanyala has ended his 2026 season after a stress fracture ruled him out of the Diamond League Final and Ultimate Championship.
articles.content:
Kenyan sprint star Ferdinand Omanyala has brought his 2026 season to an early end after suffering a stress fracture in the heel bone of his left foot.

The African 100m record holder confirmed the setback on Tuesday, saying the injury will prevent him from competing in his final two races of the season.

Omanyala will now miss the Diamond League Final in Brussels as well as the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship, bringing an unexpected end to a campaign that had produced several encouraging performances.

The sprinter said the injury was sustained two weeks before the Commonwealth Games and continued to affect his preparations and performances.

Despite the disappointing conclusion, Omanyala reflected positively on his 2026 campaign.

He recorded five consecutive sub-10-second performances during the season and finished third in the Diamond League standings, earning direct qualification for the Ultimate Championship.

His strong performances had raised hopes of another major breakthrough for Kenyan sprinting, particularly ahead of the Diamond League Final, where he had qualified to compete against some of the world's leading 100m runners.

The injury, however, means those plans have now been put on hold as the focus shifts from competition to recovery.

For Kenyan athletics fans, the news is a major setback because Omanyala remains one of the country's most recognisable track athletes and a key figure in Kenya's growing sprinting profile.

His absence from the season-ending events will also deny him the opportunity to build on the consistency he showed earlier in the year.

Still, the season leaves positives for the 100m star. His run of five consecutive sub-10-second performances underlined his ability to compete at the highest level, while his Diamond League ranking showed he remained among the leading sprinters on the circuit.

Omanyala will now turn his attention towards recovery and rehabilitation as he prepares for the next stage of his athletics career.

While his 2026 campaign has ended earlier than expected, his performances during the season leave Kenyan fans with reasons to remain hopeful about his return to the track.

articles.title: Rising Stars Draw South Sudan and Burundi in U-20 Qualifiers
articles.desc: Kenya's Rising Stars will face South Sudan and Burundi in Group C of the 2026 CECAFA U-20 AFCON qualifiers.
articles.content:
Kenya's Rising Stars will face South Sudan and Burundi after being drawn in Group C of the 2026 CECAFA U-20 AFCON qualifiers.

The draw was conducted on Monday, setting the stage for Kenya's latest attempt to secure a place at the continental youth championship.

The regional qualifiers are scheduled to take place in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, from September 15 to September 25.

Kenya will enter the competition hoping to build on its recent progress in youth football and secure another opportunity to compete at continental level.

Nine teams are expected to take part in the qualifiers, with the competition divided into three groups.

Under the tournament format, the winners of each group will qualify for the semi-finals alongside the best second-placed team across the three groups.

The two finalists will then earn qualification to represent the CECAFA region at the 2027 CAF U-20 Africa Cup of Nations in Ghana.

For the Rising Stars, the draw presents an early picture of the challenge ahead. Matches against South Sudan and Burundi will determine whether Kenya can progress from the group stage and move closer to continental qualification.

The campaign will also be an important test for the team's technical bench and emerging young players as Kenya continues to develop talent for future national teams.

Youth competitions play a major role in giving upcoming players international experience before they make the transition to senior football.

A strong performance in Tanzania could therefore benefit not only the current squad but also Kenya's wider football development plans.

Kenyan football fans will now turn their attention to preparations for the tournament and the final squad selected to represent the country.

With Group C now confirmed, the Rising Stars have a clear path ahead as they prepare to face South Sudan and Burundi in their bid for a place in the knockout stage.

articles.title: Kenya Police Bullets Miss CAF Ticket After Extra-Time Final Defeat
articles.desc: Kenya Police Bullets lost 1-0 to Kawempe Muslim after extra time, missing out on the CAF Women's Champions League.
articles.content:
Kenya Police Bullets have missed out on a place in the CAF Women's Champions League after losing 1-0 to Uganda's Kawempe Muslim Ladies in the CECAFA qualifiers final in Kigali.

The tightly contested final remained goalless after 90 minutes, with neither side able to find the breakthrough during normal time.

The decisive moment came in the 100th minute of extra time when Kawempe captain Agnes Nabukenya scored from close range to put the Ugandan side ahead.

Kenya Police Bullets pushed for an equaliser but were unable to find a way back before the final whistle, ending their hopes of securing the region's ticket to the continental competition.

The defeat will be particularly painful for the Kenyan champions after a strong run through the regional qualifiers. Police Bullets reached the final following an impressive 5-0 victory over South Sudan's Yei Joint Stars in the semi-finals.

The campaign had given the team a real opportunity to compete among Africa's leading women's clubs, but the final proved to be one step too far.

For Kenyan women's football, the result is a reminder of how narrow the margins can be in regional competition. A single goal separated Police Bullets from continental qualification after a hard-fought 100 minutes of football.

The loss also means Kawempe Muslim Ladies will represent the CECAFA region at the 2026 CAF Women's Champions League.

Despite the disappointment, Kenya Police Bullets leave the qualifiers having demonstrated their ability to compete strongly against some of the region's leading women's teams.

Their journey to the final included a dominant semi-final performance and showed the growing strength of Kenya's domestic women's game.

Attention will now turn to the club's next campaign and whether the experience gained in Kigali can help Police Bullets make another push for continental qualification.

For supporters, the immediate feeling will be one of heartbreak. But reaching another major regional final also underlines that the Kenyan champions remain among the teams capable of challenging for bigger honours in the future.

articles.title: Kenya Police Bullets Reach CECAFA Final After 5-0 Win Over Yei Joint Stars
articles.desc: Kenya Police Bullets thrashed Yei Joint Stars 5-0 in Kigali to reach the CECAFA qualifiers final and move closer to CAF Women's Champions League qualification.
articles.content:
Kenya Police Bullets have booked their place in the final of the CAF Women's Champions League CECAFA qualifiers after a commanding 5-0 victory over South Sudan's Yei Joint Stars in Kigali, Rwanda.

The Kenyan side produced a dominant performance in Saturday's semi-final at Kigali Pele Stadium, securing a place in the regional final and keeping their hopes of reaching the CAF Women's Champions League alive.

The result is a major step for Kenya Police Bullets, who have been among the leading sides in the regional competition and entered the knockout stage with confidence after their earlier performances.

Their emphatic semi-final victory now puts them one match away from securing the CECAFA zone's place at the continental tournament. The winner of the regional qualifiers earns the sole ticket to represent the zone at the CAF Women's Champions League final tournament.

Kenya Police Bullets will face Uganda's Kawempe Muslim Ladies in the final after the Ugandan side defeated Commercial Bank of Ethiopia 3-0 in the other semi-final on Saturday.

The final will therefore offer the Kenyan champions an opportunity to turn a strong regional campaign into continental qualification.

For Kenyan women's football, the result is also another positive moment for a domestic club competing beyond the country's borders. Success in regional competition gives Kenyan players greater exposure and provides a platform to test themselves against some of East and Central Africa's strongest teams.

The 5-0 scoreline underlines the authority with which Kenya Police Bullets handled the semi-final, but the biggest test is still ahead.

A place in the final guarantees nothing beyond Saturday's victory. The continental ticket will be decided by the outcome of the final, making the next match the most important of the campaign.

Kenya Police Bullets will now shift their attention to Kawempe Muslim Ladies as they seek to finish the qualifiers on a high and secure a place among Africa's leading women's clubs.

The victory gives Kenyan football supporters another positive result to celebrate tonight, while attention now turns to whether the Bullets can complete their regional campaign with the title.

articles.title: From Kitui to Malkia Strikers: Josephine Kataa's Rise Continues
articles.desc: Josephine Kataa's journey from Kitui to Malkia Strikers highlights the rise of a new generation of Kenyan volleyball talent.
articles.content:
Josephine Kataa is emerging as one of the new faces in Kenya's women's volleyball setup as the Malkia Strikers prepare for a major continental assignment on home soil.

The KCB Volleyball Club player is part of the national team preparing for the 2026 CAVB Women's African Nations Volleyball Championship, which Kenya will host from August 23 to September 5.

Kataa's inclusion reflects the changing composition of a team that has traditionally combined experienced international players with emerging talent.

Her route into the national setup has taken her from Kitui to the national training environment at Kasarani, a journey highlighted in a profile published today.

The defender has also built her reputation at club level. Kataa plays for KCB Volleyball Club, which has supplied several players to the current Malkia Strikers squad.

Her selection is not simply about being part of a large squad. Kataa was recognised as the Best Libero during the 2026 Kenya Cup, adding a notable individual achievement to her rise in Kenyan volleyball.

The national assignment now presents a much bigger test.

Malkia Strikers enter the continental championship as defending champions and will be attempting to retain their title in front of a home crowd. Kenya's last continental triumph came in 2023, when the team defeated Cameroon in the final in Yaoundé.

The tournament carries significance beyond the African title. It is also connected to qualification for the 2027 FIVB Women's World Championship and the pathway toward the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.

For Kataa and the other newcomers, that creates an opportunity to establish themselves on one of the biggest stages in African volleyball.

The competition for places will be demanding. Kenya's squad contains experienced internationals alongside players making their way into the national setup, meaning every training session and eventual selection decision carries weight.

For a player who has progressed from Kitui to representing one of Kenya's most successful national teams, the coming championship offers another stage in that development.

Kataa's story also reflects a broader feature of Kenyan sport: talent emerging from local competition can eventually find its way onto the national stage.

With the African championship now approaching, attention will turn to how the new generation performs when Malkia Strikers begin their title defence at home.

articles.title: From Lima to the estate, Kenya’s U20 stars and the fight for the future
articles.desc: Kenya finished second overall at the World U20 Championships in Lima, led by Franklin Kibet and a new wave of runners.
articles.content:
In Lima, under a sun that does not negotiate, Kenya’s young runners did what Kenya expects them to do: they ran, they suffered, and they brought medals home.

At the World U20 Championships, Kenya finished second overall in the medal standings, behind only the traditional athletics giants. Franklin Kibet led the charge, announcing himself on day one with gold, as the team collected three medals on the opening day and kept the pressure on through the final. By the time the closing ceremony arrived, Kenya had cemented its place as the top African nation at the global youth stage.

On the surface, this is familiar territory. Kenya at the top of the medal table, or close to it, is not news. But this team is different. These are not the same names we have chanted for a decade. These are new legs, new lungs, new stories. And that is where this story stops being just about sport and starts being about a country at a crossroads.

Why does this matter?
Because for years, Kenyan athletics has lived off the glory of its past. The same household names, the same marathons, the same records. Meanwhile, the pipeline—the U20s, the U18s, the county championships—was treated as a waiting room, not a battlefield. Lima changes that conversation. These athletes are not waiting their turn. They are demanding it.

For the parents watching in Kapsabet, Eldoret, Kiberia, and beyond, this is validation. The 4am runs in the dark. The borrowed shoes. The maize flour and beans diet. The sacrifices that no one sees until the flag goes up on a podium halfway across the world. This is proof that the grind still works.

But there is another side to this story, one that Kenya does not like to talk about.
Pressure.
The moment a Kenyan youth athlete wins a global title, the expectations shift. They are no longer a prospect. They are a promise. Sponsors call. Managers circle. Counties claim them. The weight of “the next Kipchoge,” “the next Cheruiyot,” lands on shoulders that are still growing.

Lima has given Kenya a new generation. The question now is: what will we do with them?
Will we protect them, or consume them? Will we build structures that allow them to grow—proper coaching, education pathways, mental health support, life skills—or will we treat them as ATMs with running shoes?

And for the fans, the ones who turn every victory into a demand for more: what do we owe these kids beyond applause? Do we owe them patience when they fail? Do we owe them space to be human, not just medals?
The World U20 Championships have answered one question: Kenya still produces the best young distance runners in the world. The rest is on us.

From Lima to the estate, the message is clear. The future has arrived. The question is whether Kenya is ready to meet it on its own terms.

articles.title: Gor Mahia’s Kagame Cup Run Leaves Club With More to Prove
articles.desc: Gor Mahia’s Kagame Cup run showed promise, but the final defeat to Rayon Sports raised fresh questions ahead of their next continental test
articles.content:
Gor Mahia’s defeat in the CECAFA Kagame Cup final has left the Kenyan champions with both encouragement and unfinished business ahead of their next continental assignment.

K’Ogalo lost 2–1 to Rwanda’s Rayon Sports after extra time on Friday, ending their hopes of winning the regional title for the first time since 1985. The result means the club’s 41-year wait for another Kagame Cup crown will continue. 

The disappointment is significant because Gor Mahia had put together one of its strongest regional campaigns in years. The team topped its group, eliminated Al Hilal in a dramatic penalty shootout and reached the final for the first time since 2015. 

For supporters, the defeat will hurt because the trophy was within reach. Gor Mahia had recovered from an earlier group-stage loss to Vipers and showed the character needed to survive a tense semi-final, only to fall in extra time against the home side.

The campaign still gives coach Charles Akonnor valuable information before the CAF Champions League qualifiers. The technical bench must now examine the team’s finishing, game management and ability to maintain control when matches reach decisive moments. 

Chairman Ambrose Rachier has described the tournament run as impressive while also reflecting on the organisation of the competition. His assessment gives the club a chance to build on the progress rather than treat the final defeat as the whole story. 

What Gor Mahia does next will matter to more than its supporters. The club remains one of Kenya’s leading representatives in African football, and its performance will shape expectations for the country’s upcoming continental campaign.

articles.title: Harambee Starlets Captain Jereko Scores as HB Køge Reach Qualifiers
articles.desc: Harambee Starlets captain Mwanalima  Jereko scored as HB Køge came from behind to beat Hearts 2–1 and reach the final Champions League qualifying round.
articles.content:
Harambee Starlets captain Mwanalima “Dogo” Jereko scored as Danish club HB Køge came from behind to beat Scottish side Heart of Midlothian 2–1 in the UEFA Women’s Champions League qualifying round.

Hearts took the lead in the first half, but Jereko brought HB Køge level in the 60th minute. Substitute Mille Gejl then completed the comeback with a stoppage-time winner. 

The victory sends HB Køge through to the third and final qualifying round, leaving the Danish side two legs away from reaching the competition’s 18-team league phase.

For Jereko, the goal adds to a strong year in European football and underlines her importance to both her club and Kenya’s national women’s team.

Her performance also gives Harambee Starlets supporters another reason to follow her progress abroad. Playing against top European opposition is helping the Kenyan captain gain experience that can strengthen her leadership and confidence with the national team.

HB Køge will learn its final qualifying-round opponent during the draw scheduled for Tuesday, August 11, in Nyon, Switzerland. The ties will be played over two legs, with the aggregate winner earning a place in the league phase. 

Jereko’s next challenge is to help HB Køge complete the final step, while Kenyan fans will be watching to see whether the Starlets captain can lead the club onto Europe’s biggest women’s football stage.
